speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your new movement disorder, can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that context. Can you describe the specific nature of the movements you are experiencing, such as whether they are rhythmic, jerky, or involve stiffness? Also, have you noticed if these movements are present at rest or only when you are trying to perform a specific action?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your description of restlessness, fidgeting, and pacing is classic for akathisia, a known side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or facial grimacing that might suggest other movement issues?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the clear link between your risperidone use and these symptoms, I am confident in the assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
